text: Kingsmoor FC empezó fuerte con dos goles de Viktor Quinlan, uno de penalti y otro tras un pase de Felix Duarte, dando una ventaja temprana 2-0 [#152] [#222]. Pero Westport Albion no se quedó atrás: Rafael Delacroix igualó rápido con dos goles tras jugadas rápidas y directas, llevando el marcador a 2-2 en solo 8 minutos [#401] [#553]. En la segunda mitad, Kenji Rahman puso a Westport al frente 3-2, pero tras la expulsión de Felix Barros, Kingsmoor subió la presión y Luca Iversen marcó un gol de cabeza para empatar 3-3 [#983] [#1495] [#1516]. Los equipos mostraron estilos distintos: Kingsmoor con pases amplios y centros, y Westport con pases verticales rápidos. Fue un partido lleno de cambios y emoción hasta el final, reflejando un esfuerzo constante de ambos conjuntos por ganar.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in es

- Viktor Quinlan scored two goals for Kingsmoor FC, including a penalty at 8' with an xG of 0.76 and a second goal at 12' with an xG of 0.291 [#152, #222].
- Rafael Delacroix equalized for Westport Albion twice at 22' (xG 0.816) and 30' (xG 0.976), bringing the score to 2-2 [#401, #553].
- Kenji Rahman put Westport Albion ahead at 51' with a goal valued at xG 0.705 [#983].
- Felix Barros received a second yellow card and was sent off at 81', reducing Kingsmoor FC to 10 men [#1494, #1495].
- Luca Iversen scored the equalizer for Kingsmoor FC at 82' with an xG of 0.888 assisted by Mason Morales, making the final score 3-3 [#1516].

- Kingsmoor FC's early lead came from a penalty converted by Viktor Quinlan, indicating a set piece opportunity won possibly through pressure or a defensive foul in the box [#152].
- Their second goal followed a prolonged 26-second build-up from a regain deep in their half, involving multiple passes including wide and central players, reflecting their 4-4-2 formation and a style focused on wide, crossing play through methodical possession before penetrating [#222].
- Westport Albion quickly responded with two goals built from regains followed by quick, vertical passing sequences involving 7-10 passes, culminating in short assists and crosses into the box—to exploit openings and reflect their direct, vertical passing style in their 4-4-2 system [#401, #553].
- Westport's higher pressing intensity (lower PPDA) and more frequent high turnovers (27 vs. 16) show their proactive, direct pressing aimed at quick ball recoveries and vertical breaks, while Kingsmoor's slightly higher possession and pass accuracy but lower pressing (higher PPDA 7.9) fits a more measured, wide-play approach [#team_stats].
- Tactical shifts late in the game saw Kingsmoor increase pressing, directness, and line height to chase the game after falling behind 2-3, signifying a more aggressive attempt to quickly regain possession and attack, fitting their style under coach Pablo Iriarte [#1187].
- Westport Albion responded by dropping deeper and slowing tempo to protect their lead, lowering press and line height, reflecting a shift to containment after gaining advantage, consistent with a pragmatic approach under coach Grace Oduya [#1459].
- The equaliser for Kingsmoor at 82’ followed a quick regain and only 2 passes, finished with a cross, illustrating their emphasis on wide, crossing play and direct attacking after the red card for Felix Barros left Westport vulnerable defensively [#1516].
- Overall, Kingsmoor’s formation and wide, crossing style focused on exploiting possession and creating chances from wide areas, while Westport’s 4-4-2 direct, vertical passing aimed at quick transitions and penetrating through high pressing and vertical ball progression. The match evolved as both teams adjusted tactical press and tempo in response to the scoreline.
